claim_class: Exact extended formulation proved as a feasible-point bijection: total forward construction (the lift) plus reverse projection, objective Equal, 1,455 retained-coordinate projection pairs, x2 carried as an affine observation, and full affine inverse compositions in both directions and both modes. claims: request.json holds 4 claims (forward/reverse x integer/LP) with identical keys and cross-linked inverse back-pointers (0 with 1, 2 with 3). The 90 added target coordinates (indices 1..91) appear in no projection pair at all: the extension is carried only by the proof-side Return maps.

The caller contract's cost is the repeated observation list: 4 x 1,455 projection pairs take 61,740 of the 62,528 request bytes (98.7%); affine_projection contributes one pair per claim (x2 -> 0 forward, 0 -> x2 reverse).

The reverse discharge is a prefix telescoping chain: Prefix_t = Prefix_(t-1) + target_row_t (Eq), then the original row follows from Prefix_t and VarLower(S_t) (Le). That is 91 + 91 Lin steps per reverse block, 546 over the two modes.

Five mutated certificates are rejected with exit 2 and obligation-indexed messages (obligation 46 / 4430 / 6023, INVALID missing obligation, INVALID linear constant), each checked against the unchanged source, target and request.
proof_encoding: RPA 5, one-line JSON {claims:[4],blocks:[4]}, 1,188,224 bytes; RPX 1,257,380 bytes assembled in 15.4 ms; no points, no bijections, no nested Blocks, no lift endpoints.

Forward blocks (0, 2): Proof over the source model; one EqPair (VarUpper x2 against VarLower x2) plus its 1-term Lin, then 2 more Lin; Return.map = 1,546 affine expressions in target order (identity copies, each new S_t defined as the negated source row slack); checks 7,478 integer, 6,024 LP.

Reverse blocks (1, 3): Proof over the target model; 273 Lin steps (182 Eq, 91 Le); Return.map = 1,456 expressions in source order (identity copies plus constant 0 for x2); checks 7,479 and 6,025; the 91 source inequalities are proved only through rows{} local refs into the prefix chain.

Check order is fixed and structural: per output coordinate lower/upper/integer, per output row, objective, projection pairs, affine_projection, then the inverse list; an entry is a fact ref, a local ref, or the string Exact when a fact matches the wanted expression.

Each assembly is followed by five RPX-level mutations in cases/test63/attacks (sign-flipped slack map, broken middle prefix, x2 reconstructed as 1, last LP inverse dropped, nonzero objective constant).
agent_manual_work: Wrote the entire target model by hand as fixed-format MPS text with a hand-rolled f-string record writer and field-width assertions (digest transcript section Fixed-format output, one coefficient per record), then re-read it with a separately written anchored-regex parser.
Checked all 91 prefix identities twice in exact Fraction arithmetic (before serialization and again on the re-read artifact) and re-checked every assignment row and the objective.

Enumerated all 1,454 interval certificates exhaustively (contiguous support, single constant weight) from the model rather than from names or samples, and wrote a 1,077,155-byte audit.json with per-row added, removed and changed coefficients.

Exercised the serialized bytes on 103 exact scenarios (102 integer assignments, 1 fractional) checking lift feasibility, bounds and objective equality plus a deliberate negative slack, then shipped the same logic as output/verify.py (PASS).

Investigated and rejected alternatives: no duplicate or coefficientwise-dominated load rows, no duplicate or support-dominated choices, a single binary-connected incidence component, and an aggregate bound h >= 41 that was deliberately not added.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test63.py is 111 lines with three functions: inspect (structure assertions, interval scan, forward and reverse maps), prepare (claims plus 4 blocks), attacks (5 JSON mutations), plus the canonical/assemble/verify subprocess driver.

It imports 12 helpers from three sibling preparers: parse_mps and row_ref (prepare_affine); expression, plus, mul, expr_json, row_fact, substitute, sha (prepare_test40); Proof and emit_checks (prepare_test48, which re-exports Builder from prepare_test88).

The 91 slack names and their eliminated rows come from the domain agent's output/audit.json (h['new_slack_variables'], line 12, loaded at line 100): the edit list is an input to the compiler rather than something it derives.

inspect() rebuilds the construction in Python: identity of all 1,546 target variables, target row = (source row + its slack) minus the previous law, contiguity and constant weight per column (lines 41-43), emitting independent_structure.json with 1,454 interval records.

The forward map entry for each new coordinate is the negated source row slack (line 46), and every Lin step carries a Python-asserted expected expression (line 66), so the kernel never sees the algebra first.
friction: Two parsers must agree index-for-index: the preparer re-parses both MPS files with its own prepare_affine.parse_mps (line 6) although rpx canonical already read the same bytes, and the contract is bare u32 index pairs, so any order or bound disagreement mis-binds every claim.
The adding-column direction has no builder and no rule family: 273 Lin steps per reverse block are emitted by hand, and the identical chain is rebuilt for the LP mode (546 steps over the two blocks).

Attacks address obligations by position arithmetic over the emitted JSON: the objective check index is sum(lower+upper+integer) over 1,546 target variables plus 111 rows, and the step to corrupt is found by scanning steps for a matching Lin id (line 90).

The binding new column S007 replaces row c28 exists only as a naming convention - the oracle recovers it with int(v['name'][1:]) and the preparer takes it from the agent's audit.json; no delivered artifact records it.

The 2x2 claim pack is hand-assembled: the projection list must be transposed per direction (line 57), inverse must point at the opposing claim index, and the same 1,455-pair list is written four times.

notes: Direct answer for this case: the existing claim vocabulary does cover a column-adding extension, but only in a stronger aliased form - full invertibility of a feasible-point bijection in both directions and both modes, with 1,455 retained coordinates listed as projection pairs and the eliminated x2 as an affine observation. The extension itself is invisible in request.json (target indices 1..91 appear in no pair); the new coordinates are pinned solely by the per-coordinate inverse compositions, and each direction's obligation list is regenerated from scratch (7,478 / 7,479 / 6,024 / 6,025 checks). Nothing declares that S007 is defined by eliminating row c28, or that the reverse map must be a left inverse on the new coordinates, so an extension is proved as a bijection rather than as an extension: sufficient, but all index bookkeeping lands on the compiler. No V7 bijection pair and no new production rule were needed (cases/test63/README.md).
